newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Q1 GNP seen at 6.34 percent - poll.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Q1 GNP seen at 6.34 percent - poll.

text.p: A slowdown in the manufacturing sector and lower growth of overseas workers' remittances cut gross national product growth to 6.34 percent in the first quarter from 6.6 a year earlier, a Reuters poll of seven analysts showed on Tuesday.
But gross domestic product, which is GNP less income from abroad, was projected to grow 5.16 percent compared with 4.8 percent a year earlier, the poll also showed.

The release of the first quarter figures later this week is eagerly awaited by the equities market which sank to 17-month lows this month on fears of a cooldown in the property sector and poor corporate earnings.
The manufacturing sector, which comprise 24 percent of total economic ouput, is expected to show tepid growth after a number of blue chip companies reported dismal earnings, analysts said.

Government earlier reported that the volume of production index, an indicator of manufacturing output in the main capital, fell 1.8 percent year-on-year in the first two months. This was brought on by the contraction production of garments, transport equipment and paper products.
"I expect a slowdown of overseas workers' remittances because of the high base last year," said Raul Ruiz, research head of Sun Hung Kai Securities.
"Agriculture and services will be the the saving grace," said Emma Pante, economist of Far East Bank.
Agricultural growth in the first quarter was a robust 4.22 percent and the expansion in the services sector was likely to be led by banks, economists said.
The farm and services sector each contribute 21 and 41 percent of total output.
Some analysts say the first quarter could still spring a surprise.
"Manufacturing is not really showing bad signals," said ING Bank economist Manny Lim, adding that good profits are coming from the second-line companies.
Socio-economic Planning secretary Cielto Habito had said he remained optimistic the government will achieve its seven to eight percent full-year GNP growth target.
The prevailing low inflation, which was at 4.6 percent in April, and the slower growth in the first quarter trade deficit back up government's optimism of a strong first quarter growth.
